records.title: Filesystem
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Reads, writes, edits, moves and searches files inside the folders it was given access to.
Good for: Changing files in a project; finding files by name; reading several files at once.
Not for: Running programs or commands; anything outside the allowed folders.

records.title: Fetch
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Downloads a web page by URL and returns it as markdown or raw text.
Good for: Reading a specific page, article or documentation URL you already have.
Not for: Searching the web for pages you don't know yet; pages that need a login.

records.title: Git
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Reads and changes a local Git repository: status, diffs, log, branches, staging and commits.
Good for: Reviewing what changed; committing work; inspecting history.
Not for: GitHub pull requests, issues or other hosted features.

records.title: GitHub
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Works with GitHub through its API: repositories, files, issues, pull requests, reviews, branches and code search.
Good for: Opening or reviewing pull requests; filing or triaging issues; searching code across repositories.
Not for: Local files that haven't been pushed; running code.

records.title: Memory (knowledge graph)
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Stores and retrieves entities, relations and observations in a small persistent knowledge graph.
Good for: Remembering facts about people, projects or preferences across conversations.
Not for: Large documents; semantic search over long texts.

records.title: Sequential Thinking
records.source: example catalog entry; rewrite from your own server's tool descriptions
records.text:
Does: Gives the assistant a structured scratchpad for step-by-step reasoning that can branch and revise earlier steps.
Good for: Planning multi-step work; problems where early steps may need revising.
Not for: Checking facts or running calculations.
